# Proto-Gospel of James Chapter 17 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** P.Bodmer V / Greek MSS, Proto-Gospel of James 17 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/POX_017_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 17

**17:1** Now there went out a decree from King Augustus that all those in Bethlehem of Judea should be enrolled. And Joseph said within himself: "I will enroll my sons, but what shall I do with this child? How shall I enroll her? As my wife? I am ashamed. As my daughter? But the children of Israel know she is not my daughter. The day of the Lord will make provision for me, as the Lord wills."

**17:2** And he saddled the donkey and set her on it, and his son led it and Joseph followed. When they had come to the third milestone, Joseph turned and saw her sad, and he said within himself: "Perhaps that which is within her is distressing her." And again Joseph turned and saw her laughing. And he said to her: "Mary, what is the matter with you? One moment I see your face sad, the next I see it laughing."

**17:3** And she said to Joseph: "Because I see two peoples with my eyes — one weeping and mourning, and the other rejoicing and exulting."

**17:4** And they came halfway on the road, and Mary said to him: "Take me down from the donkey, for that which is in me presses to come forth." And he took her down from the donkey and said: "Where shall I take you and shelter you? For the place is desolate."

---

## Translator's Note

Mary's vision of "two peoples" (17:3) is one of the most theologically dense moments in the Protevangelium. It is typically interpreted as a prophetic vision of Israel (weeping, because of rejection of the Messiah) and the Gentiles (rejoicing, because of reception of the Gospel). The detail that Joseph's son leads the donkey (not Joseph himself) is another subtle reminder that Joseph has sons from a prior marriage. The census motif (17:1) is drawn from Luke 2:1, though the Protevangelium handles the census differently and does not explain how Nazareth relates to Bethlehem.
